The .secure File Format

Explore 6 Highlights Read .secure Whitepaper →
PATENTED CRYPTOGRAPHIC BREAKTHROUGH

The .secure Standard: Zero-Knowledge Client-Side Encryption

Traditional cloud storage holds encryption keys on servers, leaving sensitive data vulnerable to intercept and unauthorized exposure. Coralgenz Global solved this fundamentally by inventing the .secure file format: every file is transformed into an encrypted self-verifying container directly inside your browser before a single byte touches the network.

🔒 AES-GCM-256 Bit ⚡ 0% Server Knowledge 🌐 In-Browser Runtime 🛡️ Anti-Tamper Header

Frequently Asked Questions

Coralgenz Global engineered the .secure format to eliminate server-side vulnerability vectors. Unlike traditional cloud services that encrypt files on their servers where keys can be intercepted, the .secure format performs end-to-end cryptographic encapsulation entirely inside the client's browser with AES-GCM-256.
Yes. .secure files feature an integrated, zero-knowledge browser decrypter runtime accessible via Coralgenz Vault. Recipients simply upload the .secure file and input the secret passphrase to unlock the original file securely.
